description: Mottled olive crust over smooth grey, dark in the seams. A Mirewart's last piece; small hurts close as you walk.
lore: The commonest stone there is: dealers do not count them, they weigh them, and a bagful has bought a first winter's boots for a great many people who came to the fires with nothing else to sell. The trade calls it a walking stone — it works between places and never during. Carry one across a long day and there is no moment you feel it; at the fire, the day's small hurts have closed without ceremony.

The part worth more thought is who keeps them. A great many people are still carrying the first one they ever took, years past affording better, and [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] has been collecting their reasons for [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]]: it is lucky, it is paid for, it sits right in a pocket. She notes that not one reason quite holds, and that every keeper can still say exactly where the water was and how the light sat on it. The first thing a frightened newcomer breaks in this country is very often [[monsters/mystical_frog|a slow green weight]] that did not run, and what they carry up from the mud is this. Kept, she has written, the way an apology is kept by people who would rather carry it than say it.
